clue.text: Type of animal one with Penny found in the rose-garden

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so the coin and the numeral sit within the flower-bed

parts.note: a rose-garden is a bed of roses
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A gardener describes some creature turning up with a coin among the roses.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-legged creature, such as a bird or a human, is one class of animal.

clue.text: What the winner of a horse-race presumably has to defend

definitions.text: What the winner of a horse-race presumably has
definitions.meaning: read as two words: the jockey who wins has had the finest outing in the saddle
to stand over a fallen comrade to protect him

explanation.definitionFit: The winning jockey has had the finest ride; and to stand astride something can mean protecting it, an old sense of guarding.

clue.text: Uses acid to put boy in the picture

indicators.note: the boy is put in the picture, so his name sits inside it

parts.note: pic is short for picture
Russ is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone takes acid to clue a lad in on what's happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uses' and 'to put' merely join; 'acid' is the definition, since prussic acid is hydrogen cyanide.
explanation.definitionFit: The word qualifies the deadly poison hydrogen cyanide, known as prussic acid.

clue.text: Gloomy Jack going the wrong way first

indicators.note: the turned road comes first, ahead of the sailor
travelling the wrong way along a road means reading it backwards

parts.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way
a jack tar is a sailor, an AB or able seaman

explanation.surface: A sad sailor heading off in the wrong direction from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going the wrong' reverses RD to DR; AB (able seaman) is a sailor, as is a Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and dreary, lacking colour or cheer.

clue.text: She barely finishes her performance

parts.note: 'barely' is read literally: by the end of her act this performer is wearing almost nothing

explanation.surface: An actress only just gets to the end of her show.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease artist ends her act all but naked, so she finishes bare.

clue.text: Is this how one died of laughing?

definitions.text: Is this how one died of laughing?

parts.words: Is this how one died of laughing?
parts.note: the idiom for being delighted is read literally, as being killed by laughter brought on by tickles

explanation.surface: A grim joke about a fatal fit of the giggles.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means extremely pleased, but literally describes being fatally tickled.

clue.text: One on a small island

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone standing alone on a tiny isle.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hebridean isle, home of St Columba's abbey, is tiny.

clue.text: Father takes part with energy of one out before his time is up

definitions.text: one out before his time is up

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
a role is a part in a play
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A dad plays an energetic role before his time runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner released early on licence is free before his sentence ends.

clue.text: Recover from a series of strokes

definitions.meaning: to regain strength after a setback
in tennis, an exchange of shots

explanation.definitionFit: To revive after a setback, and the exchange of shots in tennis or badminton.

clue.text: Helping a little, pointing to the sky

definitions.meaning: the idiom, usually negative, for making the smallest effort to help
read literally, raising a digit upward

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means making the slightest effort; literally it describes raising a digit skyward.

clue.text: Cleavage seen in Indian dress in Turkey

indicators.note: a thing seen in a garment lies inside it, so the slit goes within the dress

parts.note: a sari is the wrapped garment worn by Indian women
a cleavage is a split or cut

explanation.surface: A glimpse of a woman's cleavage in her sari during a visit to Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleavage' suggests a neckline, but here it means a cut. Scutari is the old name of Üsküdar, a district of Istanbul.
explanation.definitionFit: This town on the Bosporus, famous for Florence Nightingale's hospital, lies within Turkish territory.

clue.text: Govern with restraint

definitions.meaning: to govern is to direct or rule
restraint means holding something in check

explanation.definitionFit: To rule is to have command over something, and self-command is a form of holding back.

clue.text: The girl rebelled

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, as in the flower name
to rebel is to rise up in revolt

explanation.definitionFit: It is a common female name, and it is also the past tense of 'rise', as when a people rise up in revolt.

clue.text: Youth leader turned tail first in the country

indicators.note: the turned letters are placed first, ahead of the leading letter
the word tail is turned about so that its letters come in a new order
the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A youth captain wheels round and runs away, heading for his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youth leader' looks like a scout chief, but it is just the opening letter of 'Youth'; 'turned' is an anagram signal, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean republic whose capital is Rome is a nation.

clue.text: Have fun with the birds and be wasteful

definitions.meaning: read literally: to sport with male and female waterfowl

explanation.walkthrough: Ducks and drakes is a game of skimming flat stones across water; to play it with money means to throw it away.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a game with waterfowl, and the idiom for squandering resources as carelessly as stones skipped across a pond.

clue.text: A tax on racing here

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free

explanation.surface: A levy imposed on horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scot' is an old tax, surviving in 'scot-free'. Royal Ascot is a famous English racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berkshire racecourse hosts the Royal meeting each June.

clue.text: Servant has no right to travel round

indicators.note: turned round, the remaining letters are rearranged
having no right means the letter for right is removed

explanation.surface: A servant is not allowed to go on journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no right' removes R from TRAVEL, leaving TAVEL, and 'round' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman's personal attendant who looks after his clothes.

clue.text: See 14
Swimmer suffers disastrous rout in the constituency

parts.note: a parliamentary constituency is a seat
taken as written, a rout being a disastrous defeat

explanation.surface: An MP suffers a crushing election defeat in his own constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' looks like a person, but it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A migratory brown trout that lives in the sea is a fish.

clue.text: State needing a heavy tool to destroy the pest?

parts.note: Colorado is a US state
a beetle is a heavy wooden mallet

explanation.surface: Someone needs a big hammer from a certain state to kill off an insect pest.
explanation.walkthrough: A beetle is a heavy mallet used for driving wedges or ramming paving stones.
explanation.definitionFit: This striped insect is a notorious destroyer of potato crops.

clue.text: Filthy cones be removed

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Dirty traffic cones should be taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' signals an anagram of CONES BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene material is indecent or disgusting.

clue.text: Paddy model to rant about hesitantly

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car

indicators.note: the word rant is moved about into a new order

parts.note: um is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: A model starts to rant, faltering as she goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges RANT into ANTR. A paddy is British slang for a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is British slang for a fit of temper, a childish outburst.

clue.text: Gratitude first two skinheads give foremployment

indicators.note: the thanks are placed first, before the other piece

parts.note: ta is an informal British word for thanks
the two head letters of the word skin, its opening pair

explanation.surface: A grateful employer hands out jobs to a couple of shaven-headed youths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foremployment' is the newspaper's run-together 'for employment': 'for' is a link and 'employment' the definition. 'Ta' is everyday British slang for 'thank you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of work assigned to someone is a job or employment.

clue.text: Delving into picture-book to find a subject

indicators.note: delving means digging, so the letters are dug out from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Searching through a picture-book for something to discuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: It enables the driver to see the way forward more clearly

definitions.text: It enables the driver to see the way forward more clearly

parts.words: It enables the driver to see the way forward more clearly
parts.note: reads like advice about guidance, but describes the blade that clears rain from a windscreen

explanation.surface: Something that gives a motorist a clearer sense of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A windscreen blade clears rain so a motorist can see the road ahead.

clue.text: Body of soldiers almost close ranks

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to close ranks is to unite

explanation.surface: Soldiers nearly close their ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter E from UNITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A military detachment such as a battalion or company is a formation of troops.

clue.text: Cut down on consumer goods?

parts.note: consumer goods are read as goods that are consumed, food, so cutting down on them is eating less

explanation.surface: An economist advises spending less on manufactured products.
explanation.definitionFit: Restricting food intake is reducing what one eats.

clue.text: Not true talent

explanation.definitionFit: Crooked rather than straight, and a natural flair for something.

clue.text: Looking like Tom

parts.note: the voyeur Tom of Coventry, who spied on Lady Godiva, gives the phrase for his kind of looking

explanation.surface: Someone resembles a man named Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: A Peeping Tom is a voyeur, after the tailor who peeped at Lady Godiva.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying secretly through a gap, as the legendary Coventry voyeur did.

clue.text: The world needs love" performed on this lute?

parts.note: taken as written
an orb is a globe or world
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A love song's message sung to the accompaniment of a lute.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis 'love' means zero, which looks like O.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bass lute with extra drone strings was used in baroque music.

clue.text: Beast will react curiously by the river

indicators.note: one piece sits by, next to, the other
the word react is treated curiously, with its letters jumbled

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone predicts how an animal will behave beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' turns REACT into CREAT; the Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal, especially a fearsome one, is a living being.

clue.text: Persuade casual worker to be on time

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker

explanation.surface: Coaxing a temp to turn up punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or entice someone into doing something.
